intent.raw_query: Edinburgh history and whisky, $2000 solo, 5 days, September 2027, from London

experiences.name: Edinburgh Castle & Scottish Crown Jewels Tour
experiences.description: Explore the iconic fortress perched on volcanic rock, home to the Scottish Crown Jewels, the Stone of Destiny, and centuries of royal history. Guided tours reveal tales of sieges, royalty, and military heritage that shaped Scotland.

experiences.name: Scotch Whisky Experience & Tasting
experiences.description: Embark on an immersive whisky journey at the Scotch Whisky Experience adjacent to the castle. Ride a barrel through whisky-making history, sample drams from all four whisky-producing regions of Scotland, and explore the world's largest Scotch whisky collection.

experiences.name: Royal Mile Historical Walking Tour
experiences.description: Walk the ancient cobblestone spine of Edinburgh's Old Town from Edinburgh Castle down to the Palace of Holyroodhouse. Discover hidden closes, medieval tenements, and stories of figures like Mary Queen of Scots and John Knox with a knowledgeable local guide.

experiences.name: Whisky Bar Crawl through Grassmarket & Cowgate
experiences.description: Explore Edinburgh's vibrant whisky bar scene in the historic Grassmarket and Cowgate areas. Visit legendary bars like The Bow Bar and Whiski Rooms, sampling rare single malts and blended Scotches while soaking in the atmospheric medieval surroundings and local pub culture.

experiences.name: Underground Vaults & Dark History Tour
experiences.description: Descend into Edinburgh's eerie South Bridge Vaults, a labyrinth of underground chambers dating to 1788. Uncover the dark history of body snatchers, plague victims, and the city's hidden underworld through a guided tour that brings Edinburgh's shadowy past vividly to life.
experiences.location: South Bridge Vaults, Old Town, Edinburgh

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Edinburgh Airport at 12:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Take the Airlink 100 bus (£4.50 one-way) from the airport to Waverley Bridge, then walk or take a short bus to your Old Town accommodation. Check in, freshen up, and get oriented.
day_by_day.afternoon: Royal Mile Historical Walking Tour — after settling in, head out for a self-guided or free walking tour along the Royal Mile. Stroll from the top near Edinburgh Castle down to Holyrood Palace, soaking in the medieval closes, historic landmarks, and street performers. This is free and perfectly located from your Old Town base.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Grassmarket area on foot — a historic square with a lively atmosphere, independent pubs, and budget-friendly eateries. Enjoy the ambiance and grab dinner nearby.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and pastry at the airport or on arrival — skip a formal breakfast given the midday landing.
meals.lunch: Maki & Ramen or Mosque Kitchen on Nicholson Street — hearty, filling meals from around £6–£8.
meals.dinner: The Grassmarket area: try The Last Drop pub for classic Scottish pub grub (fish and chips, haggis) for around £10–£13.

day_by_day.notes: September in Edinburgh can be cool and damp — pack a waterproof layer. The Airlink 100 bus is the most budget-friendly airport transfer at £4.50 vs. ~£25 for a taxi. Old Town location puts you within walking distance of almost every attraction on this itinerary.

day_by_day.morning: Edinburgh Castle & Scottish Crown Jewels Tour — arrive when doors open (9:30am) to beat the crowds. Explore the iconic fortress perched on volcanic rock, view the Scottish Crown Jewels, the Stone of Destiny, and enjoy panoramic views over the city. Book tickets in advance online to save time and sometimes money (adult entry ~£17.50–£19.50).
day_by_day.afternoon: Scotch Whisky Experience & Tasting — conveniently located right next to the castle on the Royal Mile. Take the immersive barrel-ride tour through the whisky-making process and enjoy a guided tasting of Scotch whisky styles. The Silver Tour is the most budget-friendly option (~£17–£19) and includes a dram. A must-do for whisky enthusiasts.
day_by_day.evening: Walk back down the Royal Mile and explore Victoria Street — one of Edinburgh's most photogenic curved streets. Browse independent shops before settling in for the evening.

meals.breakfast: Mimi's Bakehouse on the Royal Mile — excellent porridge, pastries, and coffee for under £6. A local favourite.
meals.lunch: Grab a filled roll or pie from Greggs or a local bakery on the Royal Mile for £3–£5 to keep costs low after the morning entrance fees.
meals.dinner: Howies Restaurant on Victoria Street offers a pre-theatre set menu (2 courses ~£15–£17) — great value for Scottish cuisine including haggis and local fish dishes.

day_by_day.notes: Day 2 is your highest-spend day due to castle and whisky experience entry fees — budget roughly £35–£40 for activities. Book Edinburgh Castle tickets online in advance to avoid queues and potential price increases at the door. The castle and Whisky Experience are within 2 minutes' walk of each other.

day_by_day.morning: Underground Vaults & Dark History Tour — descend into Edinburgh's eerie South Bridge Vaults, a labyrinth of underground chambers dating to 1788. Mercat Tours and Sandeman's both offer guided vault tours; Mercat Tours' daytime vault experience runs ~£14–£16 and is excellent for history lovers. Book ahead online.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arthur's Seat Hike — head to Holyrood Park (free entry) and hike up to the summit of Arthur's Seat, an ancient volcano offering spectacular 360-degree views of Edinburgh and the Firth of Forth. The main path takes about 45 minutes to an hour up. Wear sturdy shoes and bring water.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Scottish Parliament building exterior (free) and the Palace of Holyroodhouse exterior at the bottom of the Royal Mile before heading back. Relax and enjoy a quiet evening in the Old Town.

meals.breakfast: Brew Lab Coffee on South College Street — specialty coffee and simple breakfast items for £5–£7. A favourite with locals.
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic for Arthur's Seat — grab supplies from a Lidl or Co-op supermarket (sandwiches, fruit, snacks) for under £5. Eat at the summit for unforgettable views.
meals.dinner: Cannonball Restaurant has a budget bar menu, or try The Royal McGregor on the Royal Mile for affordable Scottish classics like cullen skink soup and stovies for £10–£13.

day_by_day.notes: Arthur's Seat is free and one of Edinburgh's absolute highlights — do not miss it. September weather can be unpredictable; the hike can be slippery if wet, so wear appropriate footwear. The vault tour and hike make for a full and varied day combining dark history with outdoor adventure.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the National Museum of Scotland on Chambers Street — completely free entry and world-class. Spend 2–3 hours exploring Scottish history from prehistoric times through the Jacobite era, industrial revolution, and beyond. Excellent exhibits on Scottish culture, whisky heritage, and natural history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Whisky distillery visit — take a short bus or walk to the Holyrood Distillery (Edinburgh's first single malt distillery in over 100 years, located near Holyrood Park). Tours run from ~£12–£15 and include a tasting. Alternatively, visit the Scotch Malt Whisky Society on Queen Street for a more relaxed tasting experience if budget allows.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Cowgate and Grassmarket neighbourhood — Edinburgh's historic entertainment district. Browse the independent bars and enjoy the lively Friday night atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Cafe at the National Museum of Scotland or nearby — alternatively, pick up supplies from a supermarket for a self-catered breakfast at the accommodation to save money.
meals.lunch: The National Museum of Scotland has a cafe, but for better value head to Nicolson's Cafe on Nicolson Street (historic cafe where J.K. Rowling wrote Harry Potter) for soup and a sandwich around £7–£9.
meals.dinner: Ting Thai Caravan on Teviot Place — incredibly popular, authentic Thai street food at very reasonable prices (£8–£11 per dish). Arrive early as queues form quickly on Friday evenings.

day_by_day.notes: The National Museum of Scotland is one of the best free attractions in the UK — allocate a solid 2–3 hours. Friday evening in the Grassmarket and Cowgate is lively; many pubs offer live traditional Scottish folk music (ceilidh) at no cover charge — ask locals or check listings on VisitScotland.com.

day_by_day.morning: Calton Hill — climb this iconic hilltop (free, 10-minute walk from Old Town) for sweeping panoramic views of Edinburgh, the castle, Arthur's Seat, and the Firth of Forth. Visit the National Monument, Nelson's Monument, and the City Observatory. A perfect, free final morning activity.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the New Town and Princes Street Gardens — stroll through Edinburgh's Georgian New Town (a UNESCO World Heritage Site), window-shop on Princes Street, and relax in the beautiful Princes Street Gardens with views up to the castle. Visit the Scottish National Gallery (free entry) for world-class art including works by Rembrandt, Raphael, and Scottish masters.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in the Old Town — revisit your favourite spots, pick up budget-friendly whisky souvenirs from Royal Mile Whiskies or Cadenhead's Whisky Shop (both offer bottles at all price points), and enjoy a farewell dinner.

meals.breakfast: The Pantry on Eyre Place or a local cafe in Old Town — full Scottish breakfast (eggs, bacon, haggis, black pudding, toast) for around £8–£10. A proper send-off meal.
meals.lunch: Sandwich or snack from a supermarket or bakery while exploring New Town — keep it light and cheap (£3–£5) to save budget for farewell dinner.
meals.dinner: The Albanach on the Royal Mile — a traditional Scottish pub with a great whisky selection and hearty mains (£11–£15). Order a dram of your favourite Scotch discovered during the week to toast the trip.

day_by_day.notes: Calton Hill and the Scottish National Gallery are both completely free — ideal for the final day when you may want to conserve remaining budget. Cadenhead's Whisky Shop on Canongate is one of Scotland's oldest and most respected whisky retailers — staff are knowledgeable and can help you find a bottle within any budget. Allow extra time to get to the airport on departure day; the Airlink 100 bus runs every 10 minutes from Waverley Bridge.

trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Edinburgh Airport at 12:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Transfer from the airport to your Old Town accommodation (approximately 30–40 minutes by tram or taxi). Check in, freshen up, and get oriented in the neighbourhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Royal Mile Historical Walking Tour: After settling in, step straight out onto the cobblestones for a self-guided or small-group walking tour of the Royal Mile. Stroll from the top of the High Street down through Canongate, taking in St Giles' Cathedral, the John Knox House, and the Scottish Parliament building at the foot of the Mile. This gentle introduction requires no booking and lets you absorb the Old Town atmosphere at your own pace.
day_by_day.evening: Whisky Bar Crawl through Grassmarket & Cowgate: Head downhill to the Grassmarket for your first taste of Edinburgh's whisky scene. Begin at The Bow Bar (Victoria Street end) for a classic dram, move on to Maggie Dickson's in the Grassmarket for atmosphere, then finish at Dragonfly or The Heads & Tales cocktail bar in Cowgate for a nightcap whisky cocktail. Keep it to 2–3 bars on this first night to pace yourself for the week.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and pastry at the airport or on the tram — no full breakfast needed today.
meals.lunch: Mum's Great Comfort Food (Forrest Road, near Old Town) — hearty Scottish comfort classics at very reasonable mid-range prices. Perfect post-check-in fuel.
meals.dinner: The Grain Store (Victoria Street) — a beloved Old Town bistro with Scottish produce, a solid wine list, and mains in the £16–£24 range. Ideal for a relaxed first evening.

day_by_day.notes: September in Edinburgh can be cool (12–16°C) and occasionally wet — pack a light waterproof layer. The Royal Mile walk is free; budget roughly £20–£35 for drams during the bar crawl. Tram from the airport to Princes Street costs around £7.50 one-way.

day_by_day.morning: Edinburgh Castle & Scottish Crown Jewels Tour: Start the day at the top of the Royal Mile with a thorough visit to Edinburgh Castle. Arrive when it opens (09:30) to beat the crowds. Explore the Great Hall, St Margaret's Chapel (the oldest building in Edinburgh), the Scottish National War Memorial, and the Crown Room housing the Honours of Scotland — the oldest crown jewels in the British Isles. Allow 2–2.5 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Scotch Whisky Experience & Tasting: Conveniently located right next to the Castle Esplanade, this is the perfect follow-on. Take the barrel-ride tour through the whisky-making process, then sit down for a guided tasting of regional Scotch styles — Highland, Lowland, Speyside, and Islay. The Silver Tour (around £19) is ideal for the mid-range budget and gives a solid grounding in whisky regions before you explore more bars independently.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Grassmarket neighbourhood on foot. Browse the independent shops and enjoy the views up to the Castle walls at dusk. Then settle in for dinner before an early evening at leisure — a good night to rest after a full day of sightseeing.

meals.breakfast: Loudons Bakehouse & Café (Fountainbridge, 10-minute walk) or grab fresh pastries from Peter's Yard on Quartermile — excellent sourdough and Scandinavian bakes.
meals.lunch: The Elephant House (George IV Bridge) — famously where J.K. Rowling wrote early Harry Potter chapters. Good sandwiches, soups, and cakes with a view of the Castle. Budget around £10–£14.
meals.dinner: The Outsider (George IV Bridge) — consistently excellent modern Scottish food, great value at £15–£22 for mains, and stunning Castle views from the upper floor. Book ahead.

day_by_day.notes: Book Edinburgh Castle tickets online in advance (£19.50 adult) to avoid queues — September is still busy. The Scotch Whisky Experience is steps away so no transport needed. Wear comfortable shoes; the Castle involves a lot of uneven cobblestone walking.

day_by_day.morning: Underground Vaults & Dark History Tour: Descend beneath the South Bridge for a guided tour of Edinburgh's infamous underground vaults. These 18th-century stone chambers once housed taverns, cobblers, and the city's most desperate residents — and later became associated with body-snatchers and darker legends. Tours run from around 10:00 and last approximately 75 minutes. A fascinating counterpoint to the grandeur of the Castle.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Canongate and Holyrood area independently. Visit the free Scottish Parliament Visitor Centre, walk through the atmospheric Canongate Kirkyard (where economist Adam Smith is buried), and if budget allows, add on a visit to the Palace of Holyroodhouse (£18.50), the King's official Scottish residence. Finish with a walk up Salisbury Crags in Holyrood Park for panoramic city views — free and spectacular on a clear September afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Grassmarket and Cowgate area for a more focused whisky evening. Visit The Bow Bar (one of Edinburgh's finest traditional pubs, with over 300 whiskies) for a considered dram or two, guided by the knowledgeable bar staff. This is the place to try a Speyside or Islay single malt you've not encountered before.

meals.breakfast: Café Marlayne (Old Town) or Söderberg Pavilion (Meadows) — quality coffee, eggs, and open sandwiches in a relaxed setting.
meals.lunch: Cannonball Restaurant & Bar (Castle Esplanade) — pub-style Scottish lunch (cullen skink, haggis bon bons) at mid-range prices, around £12–£16 for a main.
meals.dinner: Timberyard (Lauriston Place, 10-minute walk from Old Town) — a celebrated farm-to-table restaurant in a converted timber warehouse. Tasting menus from £65pp but à la carte options available around £25–£30 per main. A slightly splurge-worthy dinner for the week's midpoint.

day_by_day.notes: The Underground Vaults tour costs around £16–£19 depending on operator — Mercat Tours and Auld Reekie Tours are both reputable. Book in advance in September. Holyrood Park and the Crags walk is free and takes about 45–60 minutes at a leisurely pace.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip or deeper Old Town exploration: Head to the Scottish National Museum (Chambers Street, free entry) — one of the finest museums in the UK. Spend 2–3 hours exploring Scottish history from Pictish stones and Jacobite relics to industrial innovation and natural history. The building itself is architecturally stunning. This is a wonderful rainy-day backup but worth visiting regardless of weather.
day_by_day.afternoon: Victoria Street & the Cowgate Antique Quarter: Wander the curved, colourful Victoria Street — said to have inspired Diagon Alley — and browse its independent whisky shops, bookshops, and gift stores. Pop into Royal Mile Whiskies (379 High Street) for a browse and possibly a small bottle purchase. Then walk through Greyfriars Kirkyard to see the famous Greyfriars Bobby statue and the atmospheric graveyard that inspired several Harry Potter characters.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a live traditional Scottish music session (cèilidh or folk session). Sandy Bell's pub (Forrest Road) hosts free, informal folk sessions most evenings from around 21:00 — an authentic, non-touristy experience beloved by locals. Arrive by 20:30 to get a seat. Alternatively, The Royal Oak (Infirmary Street) also has nightly folk music.

meals.breakfast: Brew Lab Coffee (South College Street) — widely regarded as Edinburgh's best specialty coffee shop, with excellent pastries and a relaxed atmosphere.
meals.lunch: The National Museum café or nearby Mosque Kitchen (Nicholson Street) — legendary Edinburgh institution serving enormous, flavourful curry and rice dishes for around £7–£9. Outstanding value and always busy with students and locals.
meals.dinner: Ondine (George IV Bridge) — Edinburgh's finest seafood restaurant, with sustainably sourced Scottish fish and shellfish. Mains from £22–£32. The oysters and langoustines are unmissable. Book well ahead for a Friday.

day_by_day.notes: The National Museum is free and open from 10:00. Royal Mile Whiskies is an excellent spot to buy a bottle to take home — staff are knowledgeable and helpful for all budgets. Sandy Bell's folk sessions are free; just buy drinks at the bar.

day_by_day.morning: Arthur's Seat Hike: Rise early for the rewarding climb up Arthur's Seat, the ancient volcano that dominates Edinburgh's skyline. The main route from Holyrood takes about 45–60 minutes to the 251-metre summit. On a clear September morning the views across the city, the Firth of Forth, and the Lothian countryside are extraordinary. Pack a light layer and wear sturdy shoes. This is the perfect final morning activity — free, exhilarating, and deeply memorable.
day_by_day.afternoon: Leisurely farewell exploration: Descend and reward yourself with a long lunch, then spend the afternoon revisiting your favourite spots on the Royal Mile or picking up last-minute gifts. Consider a final visit to Cadenhead's Whisky Shop (Canongate) — the oldest independent bottler in Scotland, with rare and affordable single casks unavailable elsewhere. A bottle from here makes an exceptional souvenir.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Old Town before any onward travel or early rest for a morning departure. Reflect on five days of history, whisky, and one of Europe's most dramatic cities.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at your hotel or a takeaway coffee and croissant from a nearby café before the Arthur's Seat hike — keep it simple for the climb.
meals.lunch: The Scran & Scallie (Stockbridge, 20-minute walk or short bus) — Tom Kitchin's relaxed gastropub with outstanding Scottish pub food. Haggis, neeps & tatties or a Scottish burger around £14–£18. A fitting farewell lunch.
meals.dinner: Wedgwood the Restaurant (Canongate, Royal Mile) — romantic, locally sourced Scottish cuisine with foraged ingredients. Mains £22–£28. A wonderful final dinner that encapsulates everything great about modern Scottish cooking. Book ahead.

day_by_day.notes: Arthur's Seat is free and accessible directly from Holyrood Park — allow 2–2.5 hours total including the descent. September mornings can be misty; check the weather and bring a windproof layer. Cadenhead's is closed on Sundays so Saturday is your last chance. If departing by air, Edinburgh Airport is 30–40 minutes by tram from the city centre.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival & Hotel Check-In: Flight BA lands at 12:00. Transfer by private chauffeur from Edinburgh Airport to your luxury accommodation in Old Town Edinburgh. Settle into your room, freshen up, and enjoy a welcome amenity. No morning activities scheduled to allow for a comfortable arrival.
day_by_day.afternoon: Scotch Whisky Experience & Tasting: Begin your Edinburgh journey steps from the castle with an immersive whisky experience. Take the iconic barrel ride through the history of Scotch whisky, followed by a guided premium tasting of rare single malts curated by an expert ambassador. The location is a short, leisurely walk from your Old Town hotel.
day_by_day.evening: Royal Mile Orientation Stroll & Dinner: Take a relaxed early-evening walk along the upper Royal Mile to absorb the atmosphere of Old Town at dusk. Dine at The Witchery by the Castle — one of Edinburgh's most celebrated and atmospheric fine-dining restaurants, set in a 16th-century building at the gates of Edinburgh Castle. Indulge in their seasonal Scottish tasting menu paired with an expertly curated wine flight.

meals.breakfast: Light refreshments on the flight or at the airport; a welcome afternoon tea or snack arranged by the hotel upon check-in.
meals.lunch: Casual but quality lunch at The Grain Store on Victoria Street — a short walk from the hotel — offering seasonal Scottish produce in a relaxed setting.
meals.dinner: The Witchery by the Castle, Royal Mile — Gothic-themed luxury dining with a seasonal Scottish tasting menu and sommelier-led wine pairing.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance. Request early check-in from the hotel given the midday arrival. The Witchery is extremely popular — book the dinner reservation well ahead of travel. September in Edinburgh can be mild but breezy; pack a light layer for the evening stroll.

day_by_day.morning: Edinburgh Castle & Scottish Crown Jewels Private Tour: Begin the day with a premium private guided tour of Edinburgh Castle, the iconic fortress perched atop volcanic rock dominating the city skyline. Explore the Scottish Crown Jewels (the Honours of Scotland), the Stone of Destiny, the Royal Palace, and the Great Hall with your expert guide providing rich historical context unavailable on a standard visit. Enjoy priority access to avoid queues.
day_by_day.afternoon: Royal Mile Historical Walking Tour: After lunch, embark on a private guided historical walking tour along the ancient cobblestone Royal Mile, tracing the spine of Old Town from Edinburgh Castle down toward the Palace of Holyroodhouse. Discover hidden closes, medieval tenements, St Giles' Cathedral, and centuries of political and social history with a specialist guide. The tour covers approximately 1 mile at a leisurely pace.
day_by_day.evening: Underground Vaults & Dark History Tour: As darkness falls, descend into Edinburgh's eerie South Bridge Vaults for a premium small-group or private guided tour of the labyrinthine underground chambers dating to 1788. Hear stories of the city's dark past — body snatchers, plague, and the city's hidden underworld — in an atmospheric and genuinely chilling setting.

meals.breakfast: Full Scottish breakfast at the hotel's restaurant — expect smoked salmon, Stornoway black pudding, free-range eggs, and freshly baked bread.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Contini George Street (or the Contini Cannonball Restaurant & Bar adjacent to the Castle) — elegant Scottish-Italian cuisine using locally sourced ingredients, ideal between the castle tour and the afternoon walk.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Timberyard on Lady Lawson Street — a multi-award-winning, sustainably focused fine-dining restaurant in a converted Victorian warehouse. Seasonal tasting menu with a natural wine and Scottish spirits pairing option.

day_by_day.notes: Book private castle and walking tour guides through a reputable luxury concierge service. The Vaults tour involves uneven surfaces and low ceilings — wear comfortable shoes. September evenings can be cool underground; bring an extra layer. Timberyard requires advance reservation.

day_by_day.morning: Day Trip to The Scotch Malt Whisky Society (SMWS) & Leith Exploration: Take a private car to Leith, Edinburgh's historic port district, to visit The Scotch Malt Whisky Society's Vaults — a members' club and tasting room housed in an 18th-century bonded warehouse. Arrange a private tutored tasting of rare, cask-strength single malts available exclusively through the SMWS, guided by a knowledgeable ambassador. Explore the regenerated Leith waterfront and the iconic Royal Yacht Britannia (optional brief visit).
day_by_day.afternoon: Holyrood Palace & Arthur's Seat: Return to the Old Town and visit the Palace of Holyroodhouse, the official Scottish residence of the British monarch, with a private guide exploring the State Apartments, the ruins of Holyrood Abbey, and the rich history of Mary Queen of Scots. Afterwards, take a scenic walk up Arthur's Seat — the ancient volcano rising above the city — for panoramic views of Edinburgh and the Firth of Forth (approximately 45-minute moderate hike).
day_by_day.evening: Whisky Bar Crawl through Grassmarket & Cowgate: Explore Edinburgh's vibrant whisky bar scene in the historic Grassmarket and Cowgate areas with a private whisky guide. Visit legendary bars such as The Bow Bar (renowned for its exceptional single malt selection), Dragonfly, and The Jolly Judge, sampling rare and aged expressions hand-selected by your guide. The Grassmarket is a short walk from your Old Town hotel.

meals.breakfast: Continental breakfast at the hotel or a visit to Peter's Yard on Quartermile — a celebrated Scandinavian-inspired bakery with exceptional sourdough and pastries.
meals.lunch: Lunch at The Kitchin in Leith (Tom Kitchin's Michelin-starred restaurant) — 'From Nature to Plate' philosophy showcasing the finest Scottish seasonal ingredients. Book well in advance.
meals.dinner: Informal but high-quality dinner at The Sheep Heid Inn in Duddingston (short taxi ride) — Edinburgh's oldest pub with a premium menu, or dine at Ondine on George IV Bridge for outstanding sustainable Scottish seafood.

day_by_day.notes: SMWS membership or a guest arrangement should be organised in advance through your hotel concierge. The Kitchin requires reservation months ahead for a Michelin-starred lunch. Arthur's Seat hike is moderate — wear sturdy shoes and check weather. The whisky bar crawl pace can be adjusted to preference; a private guide ensures curated drams rather than tourist-trap selections.

day_by_day.morning: Distillery Day Trip — Glenkinchie or The Borders Distillery: Arrange a private chauffeur-driven excursion to Glenkinchie Distillery in East Lothian (approximately 30 minutes from Edinburgh) — the 'Edinburgh Malt' and one of Scotland's most accessible Lowland distilleries. Enjoy a premium private distillery tour including access to the warehouses, a cask tasting straight from the barrel, and a comprehensive tasting of the core range and exclusive expressions. Alternatively, visit The Borders Distillery in Hawick for a newer but equally impressive experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Scottish National Museum & Old Town Exploration: Return to Edinburgh for a self-guided or private-guided visit to the National Museum of Scotland on Chambers Street — a world-class, free museum with outstanding collections on Scottish history, culture, science, and natural history. Spend the afternoon at your own pace exploring exhibits including the Lewis Chessmen and Dolly the Sheep. Afterwards, explore hidden Old Town closes and wynds at leisure.
day_by_day.evening: Premium Dinner & Live Traditional Music: Enjoy Edinburgh's finest dining followed by live traditional Scottish music. Dine at Restaurant Martin Wishart (or his Edinburgh city-centre venue) for Michelin-starred cuisine, then head to Sandy Bell's Folk Bar or The Royal Oak for an authentic, intimate session of traditional Scottish folk music — a genuine cultural experience rather than a tourist show.

meals.breakfast: Full Scottish breakfast at the hotel, or visit Café St Honoré on NW Thistle Street Lane — a beloved Edinburgh bistro with a classic French-Scottish breakfast and brunch menu.
meals.lunch: Picnic-style distillery lunch arranged by Glenkinchie (many distilleries offer private dining experiences), or a light lunch at a local pub near the distillery.
meals.dinner: Restaurant Martin Wishart at The Howard Hotel or his Leith flagship — Michelin-starred tasting menu showcasing the finest Scottish and European produce with an exceptional wine list.

day_by_day.notes: Glenkinchie private tour and cask tasting must be arranged directly with the distillery or through a luxury concierge well in advance. A private driver is essential for the distillery visit to allow full enjoyment of the tastings. Sandy Bell's Folk Bar is informal — embrace the contrast after a fine-dining dinner. September is harvest season; distilleries are often at their most atmospheric.

day_by_day.morning: Calton Hill & New Town Architecture Walk: Begin your final morning with a leisurely walk up Calton Hill for sweeping panoramic views over Edinburgh — the Old Town, the castle, Arthur's Seat, and the Firth of Forth. Explore the National Monument, Nelson Monument, and City Observatory. Descend into the Georgian New Town for a walk along George Street and Charlotte Square, admiring one of Europe's finest examples of neoclassical urban planning. Visit the Georgian House (National Trust for Scotland) for a glimpse into 18th-century Edinburgh life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Whisky Shopping & Farewell Tasting: Spend the early afternoon at one of Edinburgh's premier whisky retailers — Royal Mile Whiskies or Cadenhead's Whisky Shop on Canongate — for a curated selection of bottles to take home, guided by expert staff. Many offer private tasting sessions for serious collectors. Pack purchases carefully or arrange shipping. Return to the hotel for a final afternoon tea and to prepare for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Dinner: Conclude your premium Edinburgh experience with a celebratory farewell dinner at Balmoral Hotel's Number One Restaurant — a long-standing Edinburgh institution with a Michelin star, offering a refined Scottish tasting menu in an elegant basement dining room. Toast the trip with a dram of something exceptional from their outstanding whisky collection.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely hotel breakfast — request a window table and take your time on the final morning.
meals.lunch: Lunch at The Café Royal on West Register Street — a magnificent Victorian brasserie with stunning stained glass and tilework, serving classic Scottish seafood and oysters in an iconic setting.
meals.dinner: Number One Restaurant at The Balmoral Hotel, Princes Street — Michelin-starred fine dining with a seasonal Scottish tasting menu and one of Edinburgh's most impressive wine and whisky lists. A fitting finale to a premium Scottish journey.

day_by_day.notes: Allow sufficient time before any departure for packing and checkout — confirm late checkout with the hotel if needed. Royal Mile Whiskies and Cadenhead's both offer international shipping for larger purchases, saving luggage space. The Balmoral dinner reservation should be made well in advance. Consider purchasing a bottle of a distillery exclusive or SMWS single cask as a lasting memento of the trip.
